title: Epidural Steroid Injections for Pain Management

criteria.criterion: History, exam and imaging support radiculopathy, radicular pain or neurogenic claudication (e.g., disc herniation or stenosis), post-laminectomy syndrome, or acute herpes zoster pain
criteria.source_quote: History, physical examination, and concordant radiological image-based diagnostic testing supporting one of the following 5 :
criteria.reviewer_note: reworded as a checkable statement
criteria.original_criterion: History, physical examination, and concordant radiological image-based diagnostic testing supporting one of the following 5 :
criteria.question: Does the note document radiculopathy, radicular pain or neurogenic claudication (for example from disc herniation or spinal stenosis), post-laminectomy syndrome, or acute herpes zoster pain?

criteria.criterion: Radiculopathy, radicular pain and/or neurogenic claudication is severe enough to greatly impact quality of life or function.
criteria.source_quote: Radiculopathy, radicular pain and/or neurogenic claudication is severe enough to greatly impact quality of life or function.
criteria.reviewer_note: kept as drafted
criteria.question: Does the note document that the radicular pain or claudication significantly affects quality of life or function?

criteria.criterion: Pain duration of at least four (4) weeks, and the inability to tolerate noninvasive conservative care or medical documentation of failure to respond to four (4) weeks of noninvasive conservative care or acute herpes zoster refractory to conservative management where a four (4) week wait is not required.
criteria.source_quote: Pain duration of at least four (4) weeks, and the inability to tolerate noninvasive conservative care or medical documentation of failure to respond to four (4) weeks of noninvasive conservative care or acute herpes zoster refractory to conservative management where a four (4) week wait is not required.
criteria.reviewer_note: kept as drafted
criteria.question: Does the note document pain for at least 4 weeks AND failure or intolerance of conservative care (for example physical therapy or medications)?

criteria.criterion: The injection was performed under CT or fluoroscopic guidance with contrast (unless contrast allergy is documented)
criteria.source_quote: The ESIs must be performed under CT or fluoroscopy image guidance with contrast, 10 unless the patient has a documented allergy to low molecular weight nonionic contrast.
criteria.reviewer_note: reworded as a checkable statement
criteria.original_criterion: The ESIs must be performed under CT or fluoroscopy image guidance with contrast, 10 unless the patient has a documented allergy to low molecular weight nonionic contrast.
criteria.question: Was the injection performed under fluoroscopic or CT guidance with contrast?

criteria.criterion: It is medically reasonable and necessary to perform TFESIs bilaterally only when clinically indicated.
criteria.source_quote: It is medically reasonable and necessary to perform TFESIs bilaterally only when clinically indicated.
criteria.reviewer_note: bilateral TFESI is allowed when clinically indicated; too vague or general to check

criteria.criterion: Repeat ESI when the first injection directly and significantly provided improvement of the condition being treated may be considered medically reasonable and necessary when the medical record documents a minimum of consistent 50% improvement in pain for at least three (3) months or at least 50% consistent improvement in the ability to perform previously painful movements and ADLs as compared to baseline measurement using the same scale .
criteria.source_quote: 6. Repeat ESI when the first injection directly and significantly provided improvement of the condition being treated may be considered medically reasonable and necessary when the medical record documents a minimum of consistent 50% improvement in pain for at least three (3) months or at least 50% consistent improvement in the ability to perform previously painful movements and ADLs as compared to baseline measurement using the same scale .
criteria.reviewer_note: applies to repeat/therapeutic/RFA procedures, not a single procedure note in this evaluation

criteria.criterion: If a patient fails to respond well to the initial ESI, a repeat ESI after 14 days can be performed, using a different approach, level and/or medication if appropriate, with the rationale and medical necessity for the second ESI documented in the medical record.
criteria.source_quote: If a patient fails to respond well to the initial ESI, a repeat ESI after 14 days can be performed, using a different approach, level and/or medication if appropriate, with the rationale and medical necessity for the second ESI documented in the medical record.

criteria.criterion: A pain and/or disability scale is documented (e.g., NRS, VAS, ODI)
criteria.source_quote: The scales used to measure of pain and/or disability must be documented in the medical record.
criteria.reviewer_note: reworded as a checkable statement; quote replaced with the matching policy sentence
criteria.original_criterion: The scales used to measure of pain and/or disability must be documented in the medical record. Acceptable scales include but are not limited to: verbal rating scales, Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain assessment, and Pain Disability Assessment Scale (PDAS), Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), Oswestry Low Back Pain Disability Questionnaire (OSW), Quebec Back Pain Disability Scale (QUE), Roland Morris Pain Scale, Back Pain Functional Scale (BPFS), and the PROMIS profile domains to assess function.
criteria.original_quote: 9. Patient’s should be part of an active rehabilitation program, home exercise program or functional restoration program. 10,12
criteria.question: Does the note record a pain or disability score (for example 7/10, NRS, VAS or ODI)?

criteria.criterion: An initial injection of contrast is required to confirm epidural placement, unless the patient has a contraindication to contrast. The subsequent epidural steroid injections should include corticosteroids and may be combined with anesthetics or saline.
criteria.source_quote: 7. An initial injection of contrast is required to confirm epidural placement, unless the patient has a contraindication to contrast. The subsequent epidural steroid injections should include corticosteroids and may be combined with anesthetics or saline.

criteria.criterion: ESIs should be performed in conjunction with conservative treatments.

criteria.criterion: It is not considered medically reasonable and necessary to perform multiple blocks (ESI, sympathetic blocks, facet blocks, trigger point injections etc.) during the same session as ESIs, with the exception of a facet synovial cyst and ESI performed in the same session.

criteria.criterion: The patient must have radiculopathy
criteria.source_quote: Radiculopathy – Radiating neuropathic pain causally related to the spinal nerve root irritation, which extends distally, producing neuropathic pain in a myotomal or dermatomal pattern.

decision_rule.explanation: Policy indications are joined with AND; image guidance, no routine sedation, a documented pain scale and the session limits are also required.

question_note: Each kept criterion is asked as a yes/no question about the note. 'met_if' says which answer satisfies the criterion; 'if_not_mentioned' is used when the note is silent (silence is fine for prohibitions such as sedation, but not for required findings).
